title: Chicken Saltimbocca
description:
“Chicken Jump Into Your Mouth” How can you resist a dish like this? Easy to make, done quickly, and, most of all, delicious!
You can make this with or without a little cheese (like provolone) melted on top at the end, but only a little; you don’t want to interfere with the simple, but robust flavors.
START TO FINISH: 45 MIN
Chicken Saltimbocca
Heat oven to 200 degrees. Combine flour and 1 teaspoon pepper in shallow dish.
Slice thick cutlets horizontally (after firming them up in a freezer for a few minutes) or pound to ¼ - ½ inch even thickness.
Pat cutlets dry with paper towels. Dredge chicken in flour, shaking off any excess. Lay cutlets flat and sprinkle evenly with minced sage. Place 1 prosciutto slice on top of each cutlet, pressing lightly to adhere; set aside.
Add half of cutlets to pan, prosciutto-side down, and cook until light golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook on other side until light golden brown, about 2 minutes more.
Transfer to wire rack set on rimmed baking sheet and keep warm in oven.
Repeat with remaining 2 tablespoons oil and cutlets, then transfer to oven to keep warm while preparing
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until beginning to shimmer. Add sage leaves (if using) and cook until leaves begin to change color and are fragrant, about 15 to 20 seconds. Using slotted spoon or tongs, remove sage to paper towel-lined plate; reserve.
Pour off excess fat from skillet. Stir in wine and chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits, and simmer until reduced to about 3/4 cup, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in lemon juice. Turn heat to low and whisk in butter, 1 tablespoon at a time. Off heat, stir in parsley and season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from oven and place on platter. Spoon sauce over cutlets before serving.
directions: This is good with noodles or even garlic mashed potatoes – something to soak up the tasty sauce. Green vegetables are always good but you could have an oven-roasted tomato instead.
